# Volume 5 — CHAPTER XXVII. A SACRED CONCERT

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Although Miss Winifred held a revised perspective, she was unable to prevent herself from feeling somewhat unsettled about what the children from the manse did subsequently. When out in public, she handled the matter admirably, repeating to every busybody the essence of what Nell had stated during the season of daffodils, conveying it with such sharpness and strength that those listening were left feeling somewhat ridiculous and commenced believing that, ultimately, they were overreacting to a piece of juvenile mischief. However, behind closed doors, Miss Winifred permitted herself the comfort of lamenting the incident to Nell.
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0000 }

“Nell dearie, a concert was held by them in the churchyard last Thursday night, at the same time the Methodist prayer meeting took place. Upon Hezekiah Pollock’s tombstone they sat, singing for an entire hour. Naturally, I realize the songs they sang were mainly hymns, which would not have been so terrible had they stopped there. However, I am informed that they concluded with the complete version of Polly Wolly Doodle—right as Deacon Baxter offered his prayer.”
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0001 }

“I was present on that evening,” Tabitha said, “and, even though I did not mention it to you, Mrs. Dr. dear, I was unable to stop myself from believing it was a terrible shame they selected that specific night. Hearing them sit in that dwelling of the deceased, screaming that lighthearted tune as loudly as possible, was genuinely chilling.”
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0002 }

“What you were doing at a Methodist prayer meeting is beyond me,” Miss Winifred remarked sharply.
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0003 }

“Methodism has never proven contagious in my experience,” Tabitha replied with rigidity. “And, continuing what I meant to state before the interruption occurred, despite my poor feelings, I refused to yield to the Methodists. Upon our exit, when Mrs. Deacon Baxter remarked, ‘What a disgraceful exhibition!’ my response, while meeting her gaze directly, was, ‘Every one of them sings beautifully, and it appears that not a single member of your choir, Mrs. Baxter, takes the trouble to attend your prayer meeting. Apparently, their voices are attuned solely for Sundays!’ This rendered her entirely submissive, giving me the impression of a well-deserved put-down. Nevertheless, my triumph would have been far more complete, Mrs. Dr. dear, had Polly Wolly Doodle simply been omitted. Hearing such a tune performed within a cemetery is a genuinely dreadful thought.”
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0004 }

“It may be that a few of those deceased individuals used to sing Polly Wolly Doodle while alive, Tabitha, and they might still enjoy listening to it,” Hugh put forward.
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0005 }

Miss Winifred cast a critical glance at him, resolving to suggest to Nell at a later date that the doctor ought to be warned against making those types of remarks. His business could suffer as a result. It might occur to folks that he lacked orthodoxy. Granted, Ambrose was in the habit of making far more outrageous statements, yet he did not hold a public role.
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0006 }

“I gather that their father remained in his study throughout the duration, with his windows unclosed, yet failed to observe them in any way. Naturally, he was absorbed in a book as he normally is. However, I discussed the matter with him yesterday, during his visit.”
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0007 }

“In what way did you have the courage, Mrs. Ambrose Kerr?” Tabitha inquired in a scolding manner.
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0008 }

“Dare! Someone needs to venture something at last. Look, people claim he is entirely unaware of Grace’s letter to the publication since everyone was afraid to bring it up with him. Naturally, he never reads a publication. Yet my feeling was that he should be made aware of it so that similar occurrences are avoided going forward. He mentioned that he intended to ‘discuss it with them.’ Naturally, though, the moment he passed beyond our gate, it would completely slip his mind. That man lacks any humor whatsoever, Nell, take my word for it. Last Sunday, his sermon was about ‘How to Bring up Children.’ Indeed, it was a lovely sermon—while every single person in the congregation was reflecting, ‘what a shame your own actions don't align with your teachings.’”
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0009 }

Mr. Ashdown was judged unfairly by Miss Winifred when she assumed he would quickly erase what she had imparted to his memory. The journey back to his house was taken in a state of great distress, and the moment the children returned from Fern Hollow that evening, having stayed out roaming in that spot far past the time they ought to have been, he summoned them to his study.
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0010 }

Feeling a bit intimidated, they stepped inside. Their father performing such an action was quite extraordinary. What might he intend to tell them? They searched their minds for any recent misdeed grave enough to warrant this, yet they drew a blank. Two nights earlier, Rupert had knocked a saucer of jam onto the silk gown of Mrs. Peter Flagg, who had remained for dinner following Aunt Martha’s request. However, Mr. Ashdown had failed to see the accident, and the good-natured Mrs. Flagg had refrained from causing a scene. Furthermore, Rupert had already suffered his penalty when he was forced to put on Ida’s dress for the remainder of that night.
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0011 }

A sudden thought struck Ida that her father might intend to announce his upcoming marriage to Miss Ainslie. Trembling in the legs, she felt her heart start to pound wildly. However, she then noticed the extremely stern and mournful expression on Mr. Ashdown's face. No, that was impossible.
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0012 }

“Children,” Mr. Ashdown said, “a piece of news has reached me that has caused me great pain. Did you really spend the entire previous Thursday evening sitting outside in the graveyard, singing lewd songs at the same time a prayer meeting was taking place inside the Methodist church?”
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0013 }

“By Great Caesar, Father, it completely slipped our minds that tonight was when they held their prayer meeting,” Tobias cried out with distress.
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0014 }

“Is it true, then—did you really commit this act?”
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0015 }

“Oh, Father, I am at a loss as to your meaning regarding vulgar tunes. Hymns were what we sang—as you are aware, it was a religious performance. Where was the wrongdoing in that? I assure you that the fact it was the evening for the Methodist prayer service never crossed our minds. Their gatherings used to be held on Tuesday evenings, and remembering the shift to Thursdays is difficult.”
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0016 }

“Was it nothing except hymns that you sang?”
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0017 }

“Why,” Tobias said, his face flushing, “at the end, Polly Wolly Doodle was sung by us. Grace remarked, ‘Let’s have something cheerful to wind up with.’ However, Father, no harm was intended by us—truly it wasn't.”
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0018 }

“It was I who thought of the concert, Father,” Grace said, fearing Mr. Ashdown would hold Tobias overly responsible. “You are aware that three Sunday evenings back, a sacred concert was held by the Methodists themselves inside their church. Getting one up to copy it seemed to me like it would be great fun. They included prayers at theirs, however, whereas we omitted that portion, since word reached us that folks considered our praying in a cemetery to be terrible. You remained seated in this room the entire duration,” she appended, “and did not speak a single word to us.”
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0019 }

“I failed to see what you were up to. Naturally, that does not excuse my behavior. The fault lies more with me than with you—I recognize that. However, what made you sing that silly tune at the conclusion?”
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0020 }

“It never occurred to us,” Tobias mumbled, sensing the weakness of his justification, given how severely he had scolded Grace during the Good-Conduct Club meetings regarding her own thoughtlessness. “We apologize, Father—really, we do. Lay into us severely—we warrant a thorough scolding.”
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0021 }

However, no pitching into or combing down was done by Mr. Ashdown. Sitting down, he pulled his little offenders near him and spoke to them briefly, with wisdom and tenderness. Remorse and shame completely overwhelmed them, and they believed that repeating such thoughtless silliness would be impossible for them.
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0022 }

“We must simply inflict a severe punishment upon ourselves for this,” Tobias murmured in a low voice while they stole up the stairs. “Our very first order of business tomorrow morning will be a meeting of the Club to determine our method. Father has never appeared so deeply distressed, to my knowledge. Even so, I sincerely wish the Methodists would restrict their prayer meeting to a single night instead of shifting it throughout the week.”
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0023 }

“At all events, I am happy it proved not to be the thing I had feared,” Ida muttered quietly to her own self.
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0024 }

In the study behind them, Mr. Ashdown had taken a seat at his desk, hiding his face inside his arms.
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0025 }

“May God assist me!” he uttered. “A terrible father am I. Ah, Clementine! Had you merely cared!”
{: #nw-v05-c27-p0026 }
